newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Banerj not seen as model for other sales.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Banerj not seen as model for other sales.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan said the privatization of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj was an important step forward in modernizing the banking sector, but Banerj would not serve as a model for future bank sell-offs.
Banerj, Brazil's first state bank to be privatized, was sold to private retail bank Banco Itau for 311.1 million reais at a closed-envelope auction on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange Thursday.

"The privatization of Banerj represents an important step forward in turning the banking sector more solid, more efficient and more compatible with the challenges of the twenty-first century," Malan said at a lunch with bankers in Rio de Janeiro. "I hope this process will continue.
"With regard to Banespa and other state-owned banks, every case is a case in itself," he added.

Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola, who was accompanying Malan, said in the case of Sao Paulo state bank Banespa it was probably not necessary to follow the example of Banerj and split off the bank's healthy assets to sell them off.

He said once the Senate had approved a deal restructuring Sao Paulo state's debt with the federal government a financial institution would be hired to assess Banespa and run the bank ahead of its privatization.

Malan also said the Central Bank's PROER program, created in November 1995 to encourage bank mergers and acquisitions in Brazil's overcrowded banking industry, would be scrapped shortly, but he gave no exact date. ((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
